## RCA (Phase 1 complete): all three reds are WRONG ORACLES; the rebar defect is a SEPARATE silent drop

Re-measured against live run **30951453979** (`main` @ d394a70529). Two of the ticket's own premises
were contradicted by the evidence and are corrected below.

### The three cells, with the live failure text as the oracle

Extracted from run 30951453979's log, not inferred:

| cell | failing line | actual failure |
|---|---|---|
| `test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | :1664 — `dc_transport.set_parent(child, second)`, which is **SETUP**, not the subject | `NotImplementedError` from `_hierarchy.py:190` — "asked for `RBJREXN-2` … a fresh read still reports `RBJREXN-1`" |
| `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | :1997 — the mutation under test | same `NotImplementedError`, keys `RBJVZQW-3`/`-2`/`-1` |
| `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` | the terminal oracle | `AssertionError` — `RBJUFQU-2` still carries `fields.parent = RBJUFQU-1` |

**Platform half (1a9f) RE-CONFIRMED, not inherited.** The first two failure messages ARE the
measurement: rebar asked for a new parent, Jira accepted, a fresh REST read still reported the old
one. That is req-0056/req-0058 reproduced live in this run. `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md:68-74`
holds.

The third is a DIFFERENT mechanism: `set_parent(subtask, None)` writes `{"parent": None}`
(`_hierarchy.py:169`), DC answers **400** (`capability-map:81`, req-0055), `dispatch_one.py:594-601`
swallows it with a warning + `outbound-parent-failed` alert, and the remote parent survives. The
8b25 guard is **not** implicated — a locally detached ticket takes `_resolve_local_parent`'s
`(True, None)` branch at `outbound_field_diff.py:145`, never the non-epic suppression at :138-139.

**Legitimacy: `intended-behavior` for all three.** Each asserts an operation the platform is
measured not to perform, so each is a wrong oracle, not a rebar defect. Re-homing is the remedy
(AC4 already authorises it). Cell 3 is self-contradicted inside its own file:
`test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` installs a pin at :1810-1817 asserting
`pytest.raises(Exception)` on exactly `set_parent(subtask_child, None)` — one of the two must be red.

### CORRECTION 1 — 39c1's emit/apply disjointness is ALREADY CLOSED

The ticket says "the two gates are disjoint, so no reconcile pass can carry a parent-set on DC at
all." That was true when filed and is now false. `set_parent`'s non-sub-task branch writes the
discovered Epic Link field (`_hierarchy.py:147-168`, change 1311), and the overlap is pinned on
**both** sides: unit `test_dc_epic_link_parent_39c1.py:296` and — decisively — live
`test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS`, **PASSED in run 30951453979**.
A reconcile pass demonstrably emits and lands a parent on DC today.

### CORRECTION 2 — 4b9e's BLOCKING UNKNOWN is already answered, green, in the same run

4b9e held its Rank 1 cell unwritten pending a probe of whether `{epic_link: None}` clears on DC.
**Two cells in run 30951453979 already answer YES, both PASSED:**
`test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` (whose final assertion is literally
`set_parent(child, None)` then `assert not cleared`) and `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`
(an Epic Link clear round-tripping inbound). The probe was answering a question the harness had
already answered. 4b9e's Rank 1 re-home is unblocked and its "if it does NOT clear" branch is moot.

### The ACTUAL rebar defect — confirmed, and it is not what makes the three cells red

> `_resolve_local_parent` (`outbound_field_diff.py:138-139`) returns `(False, None)` for a non-epic
> parent — **byte-identical to :142's "unbound this pass, retry next pass"** — with no log call of
> any kind. The caller at :383-385 does nothing when `not present`. So a user's parent edit against
> a non-epic parent never enters `fields`, `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent` (:523) never
> runs, and the whole `record_parent_divergence` / `bridge_alerts` apparatus
> (`pass_io.py:103-146`) is **structurally unreachable**. The pass exits 0 and reports convergence.

Runtime-confirmed (not read off the source) — driving the function directly:

```
_resolve_local_parent(non-epic parent) = (False, None)
_resolve_local_parent(unbound parent)  = (False, None)   <- INDISTINGUISHABLE
_resolve_local_parent(epic parent)     = (True, 'DC-1')
_resolve_local_parent(detached)        = (True, None)
_parent_clear_is_managed(unmanaged)    = False
```

**Legitimacy: `incomplete-implementation` of 39c1 AC4**, cited to the project's own contract:
`pass_io.py:113-118` — "a log line is not a signal: the pass still exits 0 and **nothing durable
says the hierarchy diverged**" — and `dispatch_one.py:561-564` — "Warn-and-continue alone is why
'the parent never reached the tracker' stayed invisible through **five instances of this class**."
39c1 wired that contract into apply-time failure and left emit-time suppression silent, which is
the same operator-visible outcome. No test anywhere asserts a signal for the suppressed case
(`record_parent_divergence` has **zero** references in `tests/`).

Also found: the 8b25 guard's stated rationale ("Jira rejects a non-epic parent with 400") is
scoped to next-gen Cloud in `dispatch_one.py:554-556`, but the guard itself is **unconditional** and
its docstring advertises "no vendor dependency" (`outbound_field_diff.py:122-123`). On DC a
sub-task's parent is legitimately a standard issue and DC does not 400 it — it accept-and-ignores.

### Fix plan

1. **Make the emit-side suppression LOUD without lifting 8b25's guard.** `_resolve_local_parent`
   gains an optional sink parameter (additive — two existing tests destructure the 2-tuple and one
   asserts `== (False, None)`, so the signature must not change); the caller records
   `(jira_key, "parent")` into the EXISTING `dropped_field_sink`, which
   `run_differs._emit_outbound_field_alerts:98` already turns into a deduped
   `outbound-field-dropped` bridge alert. The field is still omitted — no write DC would ignore is
   ever issued. Zero new plumbing, reuses the acd0 precedent.
2. **Re-home cell 1** (`inbound_set_subtask_parent`) to an Epic Link re-parent: child under epic A,
   DC-side move to epic B, inbound pass must move `.parent_id` to B's local id. Same proven-green
   mechanism as `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`, and the subject (rebar's inbound pass) is
   preserved — only the impossible SETUP changes.
3. **Re-home cell 2** (`outbound_set_subtask_parent`) to the claim that is still unasserted
   anywhere: a parent DC cannot represent for this child shape must surface a bridge alert naming
   the reason, not vanish. Re-homing it to "epic parent outbound" would be a pure duplicate of two
   already-green cells; this keeps direction and operation and asserts AC3's user-visible outcome.
4. **4b9e / cell 3** — re-home to the Epic Link clear with rebar PRIMING the parent so
   `should_propagate_removal` sees a MANAGED ref (4b9e already identified this gate correctly).

No cell is deleted, skipped, or xfailed.

## Gerrit 1398 pushed — RED->GREEN evidence and gate results

**Change 1398** (`9f26: report a dropped parent, don't lose it`), 4 files:

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py` | +31/-2 — `_resolve_local_parent` gains two keyword-only optional params and records `(jira_key, "parent")` on the existing `dropped_field_sink` when a BOUND non-epic parent is suppressed |
| `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_emit_suppression_is_loud_9f26.py` | new, 7 cells — the held-out RED oracle |
| `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` | the two re-homed live cells |
| `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` | +32 — the re-measured verdict with run id 30951453979 |

### The signature had to stay a 2-tuple

Two existing tests destructure `_resolve_local_parent`'s return and one asserts `== (False, None)`
exactly (`test_dc_live_oracles_discriminate_5200.py`, `test_dc_epic_link_parent_39c1.py`). A
3-tuple would have broken both, so the signal is an additive optional parameter. That is the
caller-dependency sweep result: those callers depend on the SUPPRESSION behaviour, which is
preserved — the parent is still omitted — so they are incidental to the change.

### RED -> GREEN, held out and mutation-checked

The oracle was moved OUT of the working tree before the implementer was launched; it only ever
saw the contract card (postcondition + 7 invariants), never the assertions or the path.

* **RED** (fix absent): 2 failed / 5 passed — failing on `dropped=[]`, the target assertion, not
  an import or fixture error. The 5 passing are invariant guards that must NOT change.
* **GREEN** (fix applied, oracle restored): 7 passed.
* **Mutation M1** — re-seed the exact root cause (bare silent `return (False, None)`): back to
  **2 failed**.
* **Mutation M2** — record UNCONDITIONALLY, collapsing the bound/unbound distinction: **1 failed**,
  the negative control.

M2 is worth recording as a process note: **it did NOT kill the first version of the oracle.** My
negative control used an *epic* unbound parent, which never enters the guarded branch at all, so a
fix that appended unconditionally would have passed. I reverted the fix, added a NON-epic unbound
case, re-proved RED in that final form, then re-applied — the strict order, because a test edited
alongside a fix proves nothing. The oracle was genuinely weaker than I claimed until that round.

### Gate exit codes (real, not piped through tail)

`make lint` **0** · `make typecheck` **0** (mypy, 432 files) ·
`pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` **0** —
10200 passed, 38 skipped (baseline on this worktree was 10185 passed; +7 are the new cells)

### Fix-safety audit

Restoration, not creation (completing 39c1 AC4 on a surface it was never wired to, legitimacy
`incomplete-implementation` with cited authority) · no new dependency · **no test weakened**:
assertion counts in the two re-homed cells went UP, 5->8 and 2->10, and no `skip`/`xfail` was
added anywhere.

### Parity sweep -> [rebar:8390-32f7-e4b8-48a1] (linked `discovered_from`)

The rule — "an outbound parent that cannot reach the tracker must leave a durable record" — has
four surfaces. Slot 1 (UPDATE emit) is closed here; slot 3 (UPDATE apply) already held via 39c1.
**Slots 2 and 4 are still MISSING**: the CREATE emit (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:145-156`)
signals only via `logger.debug`, and the ACLI create-then-attach fallback
(`acli_cli_ops.py:136-143`) swallows a 400 with a WARNING and no `record_parent_divergence`.
Filed rather than fixed because both reach into Cloud/ACLI adapters, outside this ticket's declared
`file_impact`. That ticket also carries the 8b25 guard's vendor-scoping doc/code divergence.

**Not closing this ticket** — the three cells only run in the live harness, so the acceptance
criteria need a harness run to verify.

## An adversarial review caught a REAL defect in my own fix — and my oracle was vacuous on exactly that axis

Change 1398 had already drawn **LLM-Review +1** when a held-out adversarial review of the same
diff found a defect the +1 did not. Recording it because the near-miss is the useful part.

### The defect: the alert fired on tickets where NOTHING was dropped

I put the recording inside `_resolve_local_parent`, which **cannot see the remote snapshot**. So
it fired whenever bug 8b25's guard fired — including when the tracker ALREADY held exactly the
parent the user asked for. Verified at runtime:

```
CONVERGED non-epic parent (jira already == local):
  changed = {}
  dropped = [('RBJ-9', 'parent')]   <- SPURIOUS
```

That is not an edge case, it is **the common shape**: a Jira sub-task's parent genuinely IS a
non-epic (a Story or Task), the inbound pass mirrors it into local `parent_id`, and every such
ticket then files an `outbound-field-dropped:<KEY>:parent` alert on every pass, re-filed each
time the 24h dedup window rolls. It **inverts the alert's meaning** — the channel would most
often be saying "nothing was dropped" — which is worse than the silence this ticket set out to
fix, because a channel that cries wolf is one operators learn to close. It also broke parity with
the `issuetype` sink I cited as precedent, which records only when the local value ACTUALLY
DIFFERS from the remote.

### Why my mutation checks missed it — the honest part

My `_remote()` fixture **hardcoded `remote_parent_id: None`**. A fixture pinned that way can only
ever describe a tracker with no parent, so no test in the file could distinguish "dropped" from
"already there", and all 7 cells were green against a fix that alerted on every converged
ticket. Both my mutations survived it because both perturbed the *recording*, and none perturbed
the *comparison that did not exist*. **A mutation check only tests the axes the fixture varies.**

### The correction, under the strict order again

Fix reverted -> converged case added (RED, on that case alone) -> fix corrected -> GREEN. The
recording moved OUT of `_resolve_local_parent` into `diff_canonical_fields`, where
`canonical_remote` is in scope; `_resolve_local_parent` now reports the suppressed key via
`suppressed_out` and the caller records only when it DIFFERS from `remote_parent_id`. The
2-tuple return is still intact. Three mutations now each kill a different cell:

| mutation | cell that fails |
|---|---|
| never report a suppression (the original root cause) | 3 cells incl. the alert-store hop |
| drop the bound check | the unbound negative control |
| **drop the convergence gate (this defect)** | the new converged case |

### Four more findings, all fixed

1. **The outbound cell's "nothing was written" oracle could NEVER fail.** The child is a standard
   issue, and `set_parent` never writes `fields.parent` for a non-sub-task — it writes the Epic
   Link. So `?fields=parent` was empty by construction whatever rebar did. Now reads
   `parent,<epic_field>` and asserts both empty. This was a textbook vacuous green in a cell
   whose own docstring claimed to close that hole.
2. **The re-homed INBOUND cell would have been red for an unrelated reason — and would have
   REVERTED the instance-side move.** `parent` is not inbound-mirrored, so a local parent is
   resolved LOCAL-WINS, and `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` maps `parent`->`parent_id` so an
   outbound emission SUPPRESSES the inbound mirror. Priming the child under epic A locally and
   moving it to epic B on the instance would have had outbound re-assert A and undo the move.
   The old sub-task shape was **accidentally immune** because 8b25 suppressed the emit — so
   re-homing to epics removed a protection nobody knew was load-bearing. Restructured: the child
   now starts PARENTLESS (a standard issue can, a sub-task cannot — which is why the old cell had
   to re-parent at all), so there is nothing to re-assert and the pass takes the documented
   "adopt inbound, don't clobber" path.
3. **The 4b9e clear cell went GREEN on a FAILED READ.** A 401/403/500 returns a dict like
   `{"errorMessages": [...]}`, whose `.get("fields")` is None, so `assert not after` passed.
   Status is now asserted before the value is read. A "must be absent" oracle needs that; the
   positive assertions above it did not.
4. **Dead helpers.** `probe_subtask_parent_put` / `_editmeta_ops` lost every call site in the
   re-home. Rather than delete them, they moved to
   `test_a_subtask_reparent_is_REFUSED_rather_than_silently_ignored` — the cell whose SUBJECT is
   the accept-and-ignore — so the platform behaviour keeps being re-measured every run instead of
   trusted from the map. Also removed the asymmetric `try/except Exception` around the boundness
   probe: the same call is unguarded eleven lines later, and its only real effect was to fall
   back to silence, restoring the exact bug being fixed.

A comment-hygiene guard also failed on a raw run-id citation; the docstrings now carry full
grouped-hex ticket ids alongside it. That guard is in the marker-selected suite, which is why
running CI's actual selection rather than a path subset mattered.

## Corrected stack pushed: Gerrit **1399** (9f26) + **1400** (4b9e). **1398 ABANDONED.**

### 1398 was green and wrong — that is the headline

1398 held **LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1** — fully submittable — with the converged-parent defect
in it. The bot review and CI both passed a change that would have alerted on every
inbound-mirrored sub-task in the store, every pass. It was caught only by a separate adversarial
read of the diff. **Abandoned so it cannot be submitted**, with the reason recorded on the change.

Also worth recording: `git commit --amend` with `-F -` and a fresh message **drops the
`Change-Id` trailer**, so the corrected commits minted NEW change numbers instead of a patchset
on 1398. That is what left a green-but-wrong change sitting there submittable. Preserve the
trailer (or amend with `--no-edit`) when correcting a pushed change.

### Final gate results — real exit codes, not piped through tail

| gate | exit | detail |
|---|---|---|
| `make lint` | **0** | ruff check + format-check, zizmor, actionlint |
| `make typecheck` | **0** | mypy, 432 source files |
| `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` | **0** | **10202 passed, 38 skipped** |

The marker selection mattered: a `tests/unit` path subset would have MISSED
`test_comment_hygiene_guard.py`, which failed my first attempt on a bare run-id citation in a
docstring. Docstrings now carry grouped-hex ticket ids alongside the run id.

### Files in each change

**1399 (9f26)** — 4 files:
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py` (+47/-…, the only production file) ·
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_emit_suppression_is_loud_9f26.py` (new, 9 cells) ·
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` (2 cells re-homed + probes re-homed to the
refusal cell) · `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` (+32)

**1400 (4b9e)** — 1 file, test-only:
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` (`test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips`
re-homed to the Epic Link, primed through a local rebar edit so the ref is MANAGED)

### Scope discipline held

`set_parent` lives in `_hierarchy.py`, **not** `transport.py` — so the `_paged_search` region
another agent owns (ticket 18a4) was never touched. Nothing under `.github/workflows/` or
`scripts/` was touched either. The production diff is confined to one function and its single
caller in one file.

### Still NOT closing this ticket

The three cells run only in the live harness. AC4/AC5 need a harness run to verify, and the
Verified +1 policy says do not close before the change lands. Handing back for verification.

# DC sub-task parent sync: two live cells have never passed — they are WRONG ORACLES, plus one real silent-drop defect

Filed under epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb]. Operator ruling (2026-08-04): **resolve the failures;
do NOT delete, skip, or `xfail` any cell.**

## Evidence — never passed, measured across 12 consecutive harness runs

Per-cell failing sets from every `Live External Integration` job `30834117797` (08-03 16:52) through
`30951453979` (08-04 21:14). Both cells appear in the FAILED set of **all 12**:

    test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips     12/12 FAILED
    test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips    12/12 FAILED

**"Never passed", NOT a regression** — no bisect, no revert. The harness demonstrably detects fixes
(6 -> 3 failures over the window, with six named cells dropping out at identifiable runs); these two
never did.

## Mechanism — RE-MEASURED, with two premises of the original filing corrected

### Platform half — CONFIRMED (ticket 1a9f)

DC 8.17.1 accepts `PUT fields.parent` on a sub-task and **silently ignores it**. Re-confirmed live in
run `30951453979`, whose own failure text is the measurement: rebar asked for `RBJREXN-2`, Jira
accepted, a fresh REST read still reported `RBJREXN-1`. Capability map req-0056 (HTTP 204) /
req-0058 (read-back unchanged) hold. Re-asserting mattered because this epic RETRACTED the map's
label-ceiling entry when a live cell contradicted it.

Clearing is separately impossible on a sub-task: `{"fields":{"parent":null}}` -> 400,
`{"update":{"parent":[{"set":null}]}}` -> 400, sub-task `editmeta` exposes NO `parent` field
(req-0054/0055/0057, [rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94]).

### CORRECTION 1 — the apply-side symbol was mis-located, and the "disjoint gates" premise is REFUTED

`set_parent` lives in **`adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:100`**, not `transport.py` (which
contains no parent code). And it no longer "accepts only a sub-task child": since 39c1/change 1311
its non-sub-task branch WRITES the discovered Epic Link field (`_hierarchy.py:147-168`). The emit and
apply gates therefore **already overlap** for the epic shape, pinned on both sides — unit
`test_dc_epic_link_parent_39c1.py:296` and live
`test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS`, **PASSED in run 30951453979**. A
reconcile pass demonstrably emits and lands a parent on DC today.

### CORRECTION 2 — the remaining rebar defect is SILENCE, not disjointness

`_resolve_local_parent` (`outbound_field_diff.py:138-139`) returns `(False, None)` for a non-epic
parent — **byte-identical to :142's "unbound this pass, retry next pass"** — with no log call of any
kind, and the caller at :383-385 does nothing when `not present`. So a user's parent edit against a
non-epic parent never enters `fields`, `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent:523` never runs, and
the entire `record_parent_divergence` / `bridge_alerts` apparatus (`pass_io.py:103-146`) is
**structurally unreachable**. The pass exits 0 and reports convergence while the hierarchy diverges.

This violates the project's own contract, cited: `pass_io.py:113-118` — "a log line is not a signal:
the pass still exits 0 and **nothing durable says the hierarchy diverged**" — and
`dispatch_one.py:561-564` — "Warn-and-continue alone is why 'the parent never reached the tracker'
stayed invisible through **five instances of this class**." 39c1 wired that contract into
*apply-time* failure and left *emit-time* suppression silent. `record_parent_divergence` has **zero**
references in `tests/`. This is an **incomplete implementation of 39c1 AC4** and is pure rebar,
fixable with no platform capability.

## THE RE-HOME TARGET, NAMED AND CAPABILITY-CHECKED

AC1's answer is **negative for a genuine sub-task** and **positive for the Epic Link**, and the
supported mechanism is therefore named rather than assumed:

> **The Epic Link custom field on a NON-sub-task child.** Both directions and both operations are
> already GREEN on the live instance in run `30951453979`:
> `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` (set AND clear, raw-REST read-back),
> `test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS` (through a real pass), and
> `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` (Epic Link clear observed inbound via 9bb9's
> `get_parent_map` fallback). Capability map req-0040/0041.

Re-homing changes the CHILD SHAPE from sub-task to standard issue. That is the point, not a loss:
an oracle for an operation the platform cannot perform is a wrong oracle. The **subject of each cell
is preserved** — see AC4/AC5 below — and the platform impossibility stays pinned by the two cells
that already assert it (`test_a_subtask_reparent_is_REFUSED_rather_than_silently_ignored`, and
37e7's sub-task-clear pin at `test_dc_mutations.py:1810-1817`), so a future DC that starts allowing
it is caught rather than silently forgotten.

**Why this ticket's ruling supersedes 1a9f's disposition.** 1a9f left the two round-trip cells RED
and carried the loudness in a separate refusal cell. That left two permanent reds in a suite whose
value is that a red means something, and the epic's goal is DC support **without** standing failures.
The operator's 2026-08-04 ruling for this ticket is to resolve them, and re-homing is the
already-endorsed instrument for exactly this shape — used by 37e7 (Row 13 inbound), b9b8 (Row 14),
and [rebar:4b9e-bcad-456a-4233]. This ticket adopts that framing explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1 — LIVE measurement of whether ANY supported DC mechanism moves a sub-task's parent.**
      ANSWERED, run `30951453979`: `fields.parent` on a sub-task is accept-and-ignore (req-0056/0058,
      reproduced in the run's own failure text); nulling it is 400 both spellings (req-0055/0057);
      sub-task `editmeta` exposes no `parent` (req-0054). **Negative for a sub-task.** The supported
      mechanism is the **Epic Link on a non-sub-task child**, green in the same run (req-0040/0041).
- [ ] **AC2 — the emit side stops failing SILENTLY.** A non-epic parent the tracker cannot represent
      must produce a durable, operator-visible record (a `bridge_alerts` entry), not a bare `return`
      indistinguishable from "retry next pass". 8b25's guard is **preserved** — the field stays
      omitted, so rebar still never issues a write DC would ignore. Scoped to what rebar controls;
